calendar_rows.proceeding: Hearing after mistrial — double jeopardy motion to dismiss and other pending motions
calendar_rows.date_text: Monday, November 2, 2026 — time not publicly verified
calendar_rows.court: Plymouth County Superior Court, Plymouth, MA
calendar_rows.docket: Not publicly verified (official docket not yet read)
calendar_rows.status: Clancy remains charged and has pleaded not guilty. The judge declared a mistrial on September 4 after the jury could not agree; there is no verdict. On October 1 the judge denied a renewed request for a required finding of not guilty (that ruling is not a finding of guilt). On October 21 he denied a defense request for an evidentiary hearing about the holdout juror. The defense motion to dismiss on double jeopardy grounds (the rule against being tried twice for the same crime) has not been decided. In a written opposition made public October 28, prosecutors argue the mistrial was proper because the jury was deadlocked. Prosecutors have not formally said whether they will retry the case. Clancy remains presumed innocent.
calendar_rows.detail: A mistrial was declared September 4, 2026. The Boston Globe and Boston 25 News (October 21, 2026) report the double jeopardy motion will be argued at a November 2 hearing before Judge Sullivan. Court TV reports that defense requests to preserve juror records and turn over the juror questionnaire will also be heard that day. No retrial decision, retrial date or conviction has been reported.
calendar_rows.next_note: Reports differ on whether defense requests about juror records will also be heard November 2. Time not publicly verified. Confirm the court listing before attending. Sources: CBS Boston, October 28, 2026; Boston Globe, October 21, 2026; Boston 25 News, October 21, 2026; Court TV, October 21, 2026.
